瓶.meaning: A glassblower makes a pair of glass <part>rugby posts</part> for a contest, then notices they look like a neck and shoulders. She melts them together onto a clay <part>tile</part> base, puffs, and pops a cork in the top. Out comes the shiniest <kanji>bottle</kanji> at the fair.
瓶.on: The judge drops it in the recycling <sound>bin</sound> by mistake.
瓶.kun: She fishes it out and fills it with a baby <sound>ca</sound>rp and a slice of <sound>me</sound>lon.

忙.meaning: A stonemason has a hundred orders due by Friday. She carves one little <part>tombstone</part> after another for the garden gnome museum, chisel flying, her <part>heartbeat</part> pounding like a drum. No lunch, no tea, no sitting down. She's never been so <kanji>busy</kanji>.
忙.on: Then a lorry tips out a whole <sound>bou</sound>lder for the next one.
忙.kun: She eats a smoked <sound>ee</sound>l standing up, ignores the <sound>so</sound>fa, and chews <sound>ga</sound>rlic to stay awake.

尋.meaning: A golfer loses her ball in a garden. She leans her <part>golf club</part> on the gardener's <part>workbench</part>, borrows his <part>rake</part> and combs every flowerbed. At last she cups her <part>mouth</part> and calls to the hedgehog curled in the roses: 'Seen a small white ball?' It's polite to <kanji>inquire</kanji>.
尋.on: The hedgehog is busy grating <sound>gin</sound>ger for his tea and doesn't look up.
尋.kun: She finds the ball at last in a <sound>tu</sound>b of rainwater, bobbing next to a yu<sound>zu</sound>.

粛.meaning: In a silent temple hall, a monk drags a wet <part>mop</part> across the floor without a sound. A single <part>slash</part> of light falls through the window onto a bowl of <part>rice</part>. Nobody coughs, nobody smiles, and even the mouse tiptoes. The whole hall is <kanji>solemn</kanji>.
粛.on: The mouse nibbles a <sound>su</sound>gar <sound>cu</sound>be in total silence.
粛.kun: It nearly sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>, <sound>tsu</sound>...', then buries its nose in a <sound>shee</sound>p's wool: restraint.

獄.meaning: A <part>dog</part> sits behind bars, howling a long <part>speech</part> about how he never stole the sausages. Then a <part>fishhook</part> on a string dangles through the window. He grabs it, climbs out and leaves one sausage behind as a thank-you. Nothing can keep him in <kanji>prison</kanji>.
獄.on: He runs off wearing swimming <sound>go</sound>ggles, humming like a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock.

紹.meaning: At a big party, nobody knows anyone. A tailor ties a <part>thread</part> from each guest's button to a stranger's, then makes a loud <part>call</part>: 'Follow your string!' Everyone ends up face to face with someone new and has to say hello. That's his way to <kanji>introduce</kanji> people.
紹.on: Soon the whole tangled party is putting on a <sound>show</sound> together.
